newsitem.title: KENYA: FULL TEXT-Kenya finance minister statement.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Kenya finance minister statement.

text.p: The following is the full text of a statement issued by Kenya's Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi on Thursday:

"I wish to take this opportunity to appraise the public on recent developments in Kenya's financial markets and to reassure the public that the government's commitment to maintaining a stable economic and financial environment.

As you are aware, Kenya's financial markets reacted negatively following news on the decision by the IMF to allow the first year annual arrangement under the Enhanced Structural Adjustment Programme (ESAF) to lapse.
The shilling depreciated sharply and investors in Treasury Bills and Treasury bonds were nervous to commit themselves.

The result of the Treasury Bill Tender No. 1221, which was opened today by the Central Bank, show that of the 7.0 billion shillings advertised, 5.6 billion shillings were bid for. This was short of the tender by 1.4 billion shillings.

I wish to reassure the public, and in particular the investing community, that the government is fully committed to pursuing sound fiscal and monetary policies. We are convinced that a stable macro-economic environment is key to our efforts to improve the quality of life for our people. In this regard, the following policy actions are under consideration:

1). The government, in consultation with the Central Bank of Kenya will, if need be, accept higher interest rates on Treasury Bills in order to ensure it meets its financing requirement while at the same time safeguarding price stability.
2). The government's budget programme is being revised with a view to making necessary adjustments to ensure we maintain its expenditure within available resources.

3). The government is considering initiating discussions with the International Monetary Fund to negotiate for a reform programme under the second year ESAF (Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility) arrangement, which, even after the lapsing of the first annual ESAF arrangement, is still available. This will provide a basis for continued sound macroeconomic management.
We appeal to the business community in the meantime not to excessively adjust prices for their products in order to support government efforts to maintain economic stability. ENDS TEXT
